raw_response:
I have farmed this land in Quzhou for over fifty years. My father farmed it before me. I know this soil. I know what it needs. I do not need to think too hard about what to plant — it is wheat and maize, same as always, same as every household on this road.

My land is about five mu. In autumn I put it all into winter wheat. After the wheat comes off in June, I plant maize on the same ground. That is two crops from the same field in one year. That is how we do it here.

For wheat, I buy improved seed from the village supply cooperative — the kind the township promotes. I am not going to mess with traditional seed that gives low yield, and I cannot afford the expensive hybrid seed some younger farmers buy. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and then urea when the wheat greens up in spring. I irrigate three times — once in early spring, once when the stems start to stretch, once when the heads are filling. I do not irrigate more than that because pumping groundwater costs money and my back is not what it was. I spray once for weeds and once for rust or aphids if I see them.

For maize, I plant right after the wheat is off. I use hybrid seed —郑单958 or whatever the supply store has that year. I scatter the base fertilizer and then top-dress urea when the plant is knee-high. Maize gets rain in summer here so I only irrigate once or twice if it is dry. I spray for fall armyworm if I see the damage.

I use a hired machine for rotary tillage before wheat planting. For maize I plant directly into the stubble — no extra tillage, saves time and money.
